name: costbycity.net
desc: A production web application with 14,000+ dynamically generated city pages comparing cost-of-living data across the U.S. Real domain, DNS, SEO, AdSense, and an OG image pipeline.
highlights: 14,000+ dynamically generated city pages with D3.js data visualizations
Python data pipelines for sourcing, cleaning, and normalizing cost data
Deployed on Netlify: full DNS, SEO, and AdSense integration
OG image generation pipeline for social sharing at scale

name: pi-soc: Raspberry Pi Honeypot
desc: An internet-facing Cowrie SSH honeypot running on a Raspberry Pi 4 in my home lab. Attackers poke at it every day, and it feeds real attack data into my mini SIEM project.
highlights: Cowrie SSH honeypot exposed to the internet, capturing daily attacker activity
Custom Python parser turns raw Cowrie logs into structured events
Runs on a home network built on Firewalla Gold and UniFi Express

name: Mini SIEM Dashboard
desc: A Python-based mini SIEM for ingesting, normalizing, and visualizing the attack data my honeypot collects, and the applied continuation of my CYSE 300 work in log analysis, intrusion detection, and incident response.
highlights: Cowrie log parser complete: ingests and normalizes honeypot events
Planned detection engine for flagging brute-force and payload patterns
Planned web dashboard for real-time security event visualization
Builds directly on CYSE 300 labs: log analysis, Snort, and incident response

name: Constant Hall Network Infrastructure Design
desc: Full network infrastructure design for Constant Hall at ODU covering all floors. Delivered as a stakeholder-ready PDF presentation applying TIA/EIA standards. (CYSE 495)
highlights: Designed a Cat 5e extended-star topology spanning all floors of Constant Hall
Specified MER and TC placement with full cable-run estimation
Produced a complete materials budget and sourcing plan
Applied TIA/EIA-568 structured cabling standards throughout

name: Volt Typhoon Tabletop Exercise
desc: Group simulation of a Chinese state-sponsored (Volt Typhoon) attack on the Port of Virginia, covering detection, coordinated response, and legal authorities. (CRJS 406)
highlights: Simulated detection and response to a Volt Typhoon-style attack on critical infrastructure
Navigated inter-agency response coordination and legal authorities under live pressure
Applied CISA and DoD frameworks to a real-world critical infrastructure scenario
Selected the Port of Virginia as target: a high-value, realistic critical-infrastructure context

name: CyberAI Summer Camp Curriculum

highlights: Taught sessions on AI-enabled attacks, hands-on phishing analysis, and model training fundamentals
Built a "Train a Simple AI Model" Google Colab notebook: a password-strength classifier with a data-poisoning demo

Built Jeopardy review games with a real-time Firebase buzzer system
